verses.t: The testament of Moses, which he made in the one hundred and twentieth year of his life, that is the two thousand five hundredth year from the creation of the world, after Israel had gone forth from Egypt.
When the time came that he should die, Moses called Joshua the son of Nun, a man approved of the Lord, and said to him:
Possess this writing, that you may know how to preserve the books which I shall deliver to you.
And you shall arrange them, and anoint them with oil of cedar, and put them away in earthen vessels in the place which He made from the beginning of the creation of the world,
that His name should be called upon until the day of repentance in the visitation wherewith the Lord will visit them in the consummation of the end of the days.
And now they shall go by means of you into the land which He determined and promised to give to their fathers,
in which you shall bless them, and give to each one of them their inheritance, and confirm to them the kingdom, and dispose them in their portions in the land according to their tribes.
And two tribes shall be there established, and the ten tribes shall be established according to their ordinances.
And you shall do all things without scruple and with a sound heart, for you are a holy spirit of God, and you shall rule the people, and shall save them, and they shall be a holy people.
And Moses said: The Lord has appointed me before all the host of Israel to be their mediator of His covenant, and even in His mercy and patience.

verses.t: And now they shall go into the land of their inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey, and they shall eat and be filled and wax fat.
Then they will turn to other gods, and they will serve them, and they will go a-whoring after them, and they will break my covenant which I made with them.
And they shall be punished by the nations, and they shall be a scorn and a derision, and they shall be trodden under foot.
For God will go forth, who has foreseen all things from the beginning, and His covenant is established, and by the oath which cannot be broken.

verses.t: And it shall come to pass in those days, when a king of kings shall arise against them, and shall be to them a second captivity, and they shall be carried away into a strange land.
And they shall be in bondage, and they shall cry to the Lord, and He shall remember them.
And the king of the kings of the earth shall confess and say: We have sinned against the Lord, for we have lifted up our hand against a people that served the Lord their God.
Then they shall remember me, saying: Look, the things which Moses did in Egypt, and the signs and wonders which the Lord commanded him to do.

verses.t: Then shall they call upon me, and I will have compassion upon them, and I will bring them back into their land.
And they shall build the house of the Lord, and they shall prosper, and they shall be established.
But after these things they shall again deal wickedly, and they shall defile the house of the Lord, and they shall turn aside to the idols of the Gentiles.

verses.t: And in those days the kings of the earth shall be their rulers, and they shall be unjust, and they shall oppress them.
And the priests shall be proud, and they shall take gifts, and they shall sell justice.
And the holy things shall be polluted, and they shall eat of the offerings of the Lord like common food.

verses.t: Then shall arise kings bearing rule, and they shall be called priests of the Most High God, and they shall work iniquity in the holy of holies.
And they shall fill the house of the Lord with abominations, and they shall set up the idol of the stranger in it.

verses.t: And thereafter shall arise pestilent men, saying of themselves that they are just.
And they shall stir up wrath, and they shall be deceitful men, seeking to please themselves, and they shall be full of all uncleanness.
And they shall devour the goods of the poor, saying that they do it on the ground of justice.

And they shall be querulous, deceitful, hiding themselves lest they should be known, impious, filled with lawlessness and iniquity from sunrise to sunset, saying: We shall have feastings and luxury, eating and drinking, and we shall be as princes.

verses.t: And there shall come upon them punishment and wrath, such as has not befallen them from the beginning until that time, in which He will stir up against them the king of the kings of the earth, who shall have great power, and who shall hang on the tree them that confess their circumcision.
Even those who conceal themselves shall be tortured, and their wives shall be given to the gods of the Gentiles, and their young sons shall be cut by physicians to bring in a third circumcision.
And they shall be punished by torments, and fire and sword, and they shall be carried away captive into the west.

verses.t: And then in that day they shall flee, both they and their sons and their wives, into a cave in the field, and they shall say: Let us die rather than transgress the commands of the Lord of lords, the God of our fathers.
For if we do this and die, our blood shall be avenged before the Lord.

verses.t: And then His kingdom shall appear throughout all His creation, and then Satan shall be no more, and sorrow shall depart with him.
Then the hands of the angel shall be filled who shall be appointed, and he shall avenge them of their enemies.
For the Heavenly One will arise from His royal throne, and He will go forth from His holy habitation with indignation and wrath on account of His sons.
And the earth shall tremble: to its confines shall it be shaken: and the high mountains shall be made low, and the hills shall be shaken and fall.
And the sun shall not give light, and the horns of the moon shall be broken, and shall be turned into darkness, and the stars shall be thrown into array.
And the sea shall retire into the abyss, and the fountains of waters shall fail, and the rivers shall dry up.
For the Most High will arise, the Eternal God alone, and He will appear to punish the Gentiles, and He will destroy all their idols.
Then you, O Israel, shall be happy, and you shall mount upon the necks and wings of the eagle, and they shall be ended.
And God will exalt you, and He will cause you to approach to the heaven of the stars, in the place of their habitation.
And you shall look from on high and shall see your enemies in Gehenna, and you shall recognize them and rejoice, and you shall give thanks and confess your Creator.

verses.t: And when Joshua had heard the words of Moses that were so written in his writing, even all that he had before said, he rent his clothes and cast himself at Moses’ feet.
And Moses encouraged him and wept with him.

And Joshua answered him and said: Why do you comfort me, lord Moses? and how shall I be comforted in regard to the bitter word which has gone forth from your mouth, which is full of tears and lamentation, in that you depart from this people?
But what place shall receive you? or what shall be the monument of your sepulchre? or who shall dare to bear your body as a man from one place to another?
For all that die, their sepulchres are upon the earth; but your sepulchre is from the rising to the setting sun, and from the south to the confines of the north: all the world is your sepulchre.
Lord, you are departing; and who shall feed this people? or who is there that shall have compassion on them, and who shall be their guide on the way?
Or who shall pray for them, not omitting a single day, in order that I may lead them into the land of their forefathers?
How therefore am I to take this people as a father takes his little son into his mouth, or as a nurse takes her sucking child into the land which you have sworn to their fathers?

How shall I also be able to guard this people as a father his only son, and as a mother her daughter, a virgin who is being prepared for her husband, who is in terror and protects her body from the sun and takes heed lest her feet should stumble?
Shall they then be a people of six hundred thousand? For these have grown to such a multitude through your prayers, my lord Moses.
And what wisdom or understanding have I, that I should judge or give answer in the house of the Lord?

Moreover the kings of the Amorites, when they hear that we are attacking them, judging that there is no longer among them the holy spirit who was worthy of the Lord, manifold and incomprehensible, the lord of the word, who was faithful in all things, God’s chief prophet throughout the earth, the most perfect teacher in the world, that he is no longer among them, shall say: Let us go against them.

If the enemy have but once done impiously against their Lord, they have no advocate to offer prayers on their behalf to the Lord, as Moses was a great messenger, who every hour, day and night, had his knees fixed to the earth, praying and looking for a vision and a great messenger who bowed before him on his knees in the tent, and who was heard.

verses.t: And when Joshua had finished these words, he again cast himself at the feet of Moses.
And Moses took his hand and raised him into the seat before him, and answered and said to him:
Joshua, despise not yourself, but put away care, and attend to my words.

God has created all the nations, them that are in the world, and us also. He has foreseen them and us from the beginning of the creation of the world even to the end of the age, and nothing has been neglected by Him, even to the least thing, but all things He has foreseen and caused all to come forth.
The Lord has appointed me before all to pray for their sins and for their transgression.
Not for any virtue or strength of mine, but of His good pleasure have His mercy and longsuffering come to me.
For I tell you, Joshua: it is not on account of the piety of this people that you shall root out the nations.
The firmament of the heaven, the foundations of the earth, were made and approved by God and are under the ring of His right hand.
Therefore they who do and fulfil the commandments of God shall increase and be prospered.
But they who sin and set at nought the commandments shall be without the blessings before mentioned, and they shall be punished with many torments by the nations.
Yet it is not possible that He should wholly destroy and forsake them.
For God will go forth, who has foreseen all things for ever, and His covenant has been established, and by the oath which cannot be broken.
